# Rendering scenes

`Rendering3D` draws a rotating box frame, an imported triangular ramp and a
pedestal assembled from two mesh parts. A sun, warm point light and cool spot
light shade them and cast shadows on the floor. The environment supplies ambient
light, occlusion, bloom and tone mapping. The green ring in front comes from a
Surface Influence wired to the floor material's emission.
The `RenderPedestal` prototype owns its prepared mesh-parts composition; the scene
places it alongside the other objects.

`RenderFrameProbe` extracts the frame's first beam with `primitive_part`, uses
`transform_visual_offset` to place its orange copy beside the frame, then triggers
a visual reaction on the rotating source. The `render-fixture` C case runs this
scene for four simulation steps and checks the copy's dimensions and transformed
position, the source's rotation, and its reaction lift. These assertions exercise
the authored behavior through the controller.

`PlanarSurfaces` draws a hollow SDF ring and a tilted mesh box with the same
height-colored material. Its camera selects full-resolution surfaces and
tetrahedral SDF normals. A material mask below them receives their planar
reflections. These components need the planar renderer, so this scene does not
select 3D presentation.

`RenderingVisibility` opens a circular sight region around the yellow box. The
blue box lies outside sight and uses visibility culling. The red box is inside
sight but explicitly hidden. Only the yellow box should appear. This scene also
uses the existing Vision component; it does not exercise the `Visibility At`
behavior function.

All three scenes own their cameras. The four-frame catalog coverage check runs
simulation only. Use the admitted `scene3d` and `sdf-visibility` GPU checks for
renderer assertions and bounded scene previews to inspect these compositions.
One output image does not prove temporal stability.

The `preview-components` C case checks that scene and prototype previews keep
project-defined components alive through simulation and restore the previous
component catalog after success or failure.

From the engine checkout, with `CHIBI_CTL` set to the controller being checked:

```sh
"$CHIBI_CTL" --project-root test/fixtures/feature-coverage --format
printf '%s\n' '{"contract":1,"operation":"validate_project"}' |
  "$CHIBI_CTL" --project-root test/fixtures/feature-coverage
printf '%s\n' '{"contract":1,"operation":"preview_scene","kind":"scene","name":"Rendering3D","frames":4,"width":400,"height":280,"gpu_warmup_frames":1}' |
  "$CHIBI_CTL" --project-root test/fixtures/feature-coverage --render
```

Use the same preview request for `RenderingVisibility`. For `PlanarSurfaces`,
use 320 by 240 pixels. Keep the native preview resource limits. See
`docs/agent-execution.md` and `docs/testing.md`.

The imported ramp's source is `sources/RenderWedge.gltf`, eight triangles with
flat normals, a green material and no external resources. Its native
`content/meshes/RenderWedge.mesh`, `content/prototypes/RenderWedge.kdl` and
`content/materials/RenderWedge_Green.kdl` are generated by the controller's
`import_model` operation with that source's absolute path and name `RenderWedge`.
To regenerate, remove those three generated assets first; imports never overwrite
an existing asset. The scene applies its size and 3D placement.
